substantive_reconstruction.isotropic_counterexample: For d>=2, ||Phi_d||^2=d/d=1. Its coefficient after U tensor conjugate(U) at(a,b) is sum_i U_ai conjugate(U_bi)/sqrt(d)=delta_ab/sqrt(d), hence the rank-one projector is an isotropic density state. Expanding matrix units gives Gamma(Phi_d)=sum_ij E_ij tensor E_ji/d=F/d. On the unit vector(|1,2>-|2,1>)/sqrt2 it has expectation-1/d. It is Hermitian, trace tr(F)/d=d/d=1 and common-U invariant, but not positive. The source word 'state' therefore overreaches despite the true symmetry identity.
substantive_reconstruction.full_sandwich: Write arbitrary Z=sum_ij Z_ij tensor E_ij. The sandwich partial transpose is sum_ij A Z_ij C tensor(B E_ij D)^T=sum_ij A Z_ij C tensor D^T E_ji B^T, exactly(A tensor D^T)Gamma(Z)(C tensor B^T). This proof is complex-linear, dimension-independent, applies to non-Hermitian and zero Z, reverses only multiplication in the second factor and does not assert Gamma is a full bipartite anti-homomorphism.
substantive_reconstruction.correct_conjugation_substitution: For an actual isotropic conjugation the left factors are A=U,B=conjugate(U), while the right factors are C=U^dagger,D=U^T=(conjugate(U))^dagger. Thus D^T=U and B^T=U^dagger. The transformed sandwich is(U tensor U)Gamma(Z)(U^dagger tensor U^dagger). No U^dagger=U shortcut is permitted; setting the right factors equal to the left factors would be a different sandwich.
substantive_reconstruction.both_operator_directions: If the isotropic conjugation fixes Z for every U, applying Gamma and the identity yields Werner invariance of Gamma(Z). Conversely Werner invariance makes Gamma of the isotropic conjugation equal Gamma(Z); involutivity Gamma^2=id gives back equality to Z. Neither direction needs positivity, trace, Hermiticity or nonzero Z. Trace is preserved by keeping diagonal coefficients; Gamma also commutes with taking adjoint, hence preserves Hermiticity, but neither fact implies positivity.
substantive_reconstruction.conditional_state_theorem: Fix any density rho. If it has isotropic symmetry and Gamma(rho)>=0, operator transport gives Werner symmetry, positivity is exactly the PPT condition and trace is still1: Gamma(rho) is a Werner state. If Gamma(rho) is a Werner state, it is positive, giving PPT, and its Werner symmetry transports back to isotropic symmetry of the already-given density rho. Thus the candidate's bracketed equivalence is exact. The old reverse implication is valid on density rho, while the forward positivity implication fails at Phi_d.
substantive_reconstruction.one_zero_and_empty_dimensions: Zero Z satisfies both operator symmetries but has trace0 and is not a state. At d=1, Gamma is identity and conjugation by U tensor U or U tensor conjugate(U) is scalar conjugation and hence trivial; the unique density is1 and is PPT. No antisymmetric vector exists there. At d=0 the endomorphism space has only0 with trace0, so no density exists; operator identities are trivial and no1/sqrt(d), F/d or1/(d^2-1) normalization is used. The source's nontrivial Werner parameterization assumes d>=2, while this natural boundary extension is proved directly rather than plugged into it.
substantive_reconstruction.exact_scope_and_resources: All formulas concern operators in the fixed bases, not a physical implementation of partial transpose as a positive quantum channel. The counterexample itself shows why such positivity cannot be inferred. No circuit, state-preparation, finite-bit runtime or new native formal certificate follows.
